chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abu al-Subbah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'We are a people upon whom God has made our obedience obligatory; to us belong the al-fay' (booty/gains), and to us belongs the choicest part of the wealth. We are the firm-rooted in knowledge, and we are the ones who are envied, as God the Exalted said: "Or do they envy people for what God has given them of His bounty?"'

key_terms.الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلَامِ: Those firmly rooted and established in knowledge.
key_terms.الْأَنْفَالُ: The special gains or booty, often referring to wealth not acquired by direct battle, belonging to the Imam.
key_terms.صَفْوُ الْأَمْوَالِ: The choicest or purest portion of wealth.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'anfal' and 'safw' for the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the theological basis for the Imams' exclusive right to *anfal* (special booty) and *safw* (choicest portion) of wealth, linking it directly to the divine ordination of their obedience. He characterizes the Imams as the *rasikhun* (firmly rooted) in knowledge, thereby justifying the envy mentioned in the Quranic verse as a natural reaction to the unique spiritual and material blessings bestowed upon them by God.
